To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ping-pong ball is an interesting object for real-time vision guided acting of industrial robot arms and that a physically correct model is needed in order to catch the ball.
a robot arm can be controlled by vision and that the flight of a ball can be modeled in real-time.
a robot arm can catch and juggle a ping-pong-ball with the help of vision and a novel non-linear flight model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the standard industrial robot can be used as a general-purpose manipulator in a human environment.
a vision guided robot arm that is able to perform a complex task that is not possible for humans.
the question of how to control an industrial robot arm by the means of vision and how to model the flight dynamics of the ball in order to solve a real-time ball-catching task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-linear model of the ball's motion is necessary to solve the catching task.
the non-linear model of the ball's trajectory is the most important ingredient for the successful real-time implementation of a vision guided robot juggling system.
the non-linear model of the ball's flight trajectory, the real-time vision system and the real-time robot control are the main factors for the success of the ping-pong ball robot.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a real-time framework for the control of industrial robots by vision is feasible.
the naive linear model is sufficient for a juggling task, but the non-linear model has to be used for the more demanding initial catching task.
the naive model is good for juggling and the physically correct model is good for catching, which makes the combination of both models a good choice for both tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the juggling task can be solved with a standard industrial robot arm and standard industrial cameras.
a standard industrial robot arm can be controlled in real-time to catch and juggle ping-pong balls.

a real-time vision system for a robot can be implemented with a low-cost hardware platform, and that the performance of the system can be improved with a physically correct model of a ball flight trajectory.
